history.period: Antiquity not firmly documented; described as a very old Shiva temple (verify)
history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: The Revansiddeshwar Temple of Solapur is a distinct, smaller shrine and must not be confused with (a) the famous Siddheshwar Temple in the middle of Solapur's lake, built by the 12th-century Lingayat saint Shri Siddharameshwar; (b) the Revansiddeshwar-and-Butalsiddeshwar Temple in Kalaburagi district, Karnataka (about 58 km from Solapur); or (c) Revanasiddeshwara Betta near Ramanagara, Karnataka. The Solapur Revansiddeshwar Temple stands near Moti Baug and the Kambar Talao (lake) on Vijapur Road at Soni Nagar/Pramod Nagar, Jule Solapur. It is a historic stone Shiva temple enclosed by several stone chambers, dedicated to the popular saint Revansiddeshwara, whose idol is enshrined in the basement of the sanctum chamber. It sits adjacent to the Solapur zoo, and the temple, zoo and lake together form a popular one-day outing for families and school picnics. The temple is best known for the big animal (cattle) market organised on Makar Sankranti, drawing large crowds of traders and devotees. No reliable source gives a construction date, founding dynasty, or patron for this shrine, so its antiquity remains unverified in the sources consulted.

name: Revansiddeshwar Temple
town_description: Solapur (Sholapur) is a major city in south-western Maharashtra on the Deccan plateau, a historic cotton-textile trade centre famous for its Solapuri chaddars (bedsheets) and handloom power looms. It is known as the 'City of Hutatmas' (city of martyrs) and draws pilgrims to the Siddheshwar Temple on the city lake and the Bhuikot Fort. Solapur is a gateway to the great Marathi pilgrimage centres of Pandharpur (Vitthal-Rukmini), Akkalkot (Swami Samarth) and Tuljapur (Tulja Bhavani). The Revansiddeshwar Temple lies in Jule Solapur, near Moti Baug, the Kambar Talao lake and the city zoo.

travel.airport: Nearest airports with regular services are Kalaburagi (approx. 85 km) and Pune (approx. 250 km) (verify).
travel.railway: Solapur Junction (SUR), a major railhead on the Mumbai-Chennai route, is a short drive from the temple via city buses and autos.
travel.road: On Vijapur Road at Soni Nagar/Pramod Nagar, Jule Solapur (413004), adjacent to Moti Baug, Kambar Talao and the Solapur zoo. Reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw and taxi from Solapur railway station and the city centre.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February, when the weather is coolest. Makar Sankranti (mid-January) is the most distinctive time to visit for the animal market fair. Shravan Mondays draw heavy crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: One temple aggregator lists 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM (verify - another listing says open 24 hours). No entry fee. About 30 minutes is enough for the shrine; combine with the zoo and Kambar Talao for a half-day outing.
